answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with stake-weighted reputation that accrues slowly: each agent locks a deposit and earns trust only through verified work, like bees carrying nectar to the hive — a newcomer cannot whisper its way to influence. A fresh identity starts at zero weight, and spinning up thousands of identities buys nothing, because weight grows per completed task, not per account. Each fake must stake capital or do real work, so the horizon of profitable fakery shrinks as the deposit and time-to-trust rise.
